The decomposition represents the tensor as a sum of three types of components, one for each mode being the "rank-one" vector.
**X-mode components:** A vector $\mathbf{v}_r^X \in \mathbb{R}^I$ and a matrix $\mathbf{M}_r^{Y,Z} \in \mathbb{R}^{J \times K}$.
**Y-mode components:** A vector $\mathbf{v}_r^Y \in \mathbb{R}^J$ and a matrix $\mathbf{M}_r^{X,Z} \in \mathbb{R}^{I \times K}$.
**Z-mode components:** A vector $\mathbf{v}_r^Z \in \mathbb{R}^K$ and a matrix $\mathbf{M}_r^{X,Y} \in \mathbb{R}^{I \times J}$.
Where $\circ$ denotes the outer product between a vector and a matrix.
